the design of a low-power, high-performance, quadrature downconversion mixer that employs bias current reuse to achieve a low power dissipation.
the design of low power and low voltage quadrature mixers for use in RF receivers.
the development and implementation of low power, high performance harmonic rejection mixers for applications in software-defined radio and wireless communication.

this thesis demonstrates the feasibility and benefits of bias-sharing in harmonic rejection mixers, and that it can be applied in a variety of mixer topologies to reduce power and improve performance, while also reducing the number of bias current sources in the design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a novel quadrature downconversion topology that provides a significant reduction of power consumption, and a significant improvement of harmonic rejection, while maintaining the same level of performance as the state of the art.

we demonstrated a two-stage harmonic rejection downconverter with bias current reuse and orthogonal phasing of the RF and baseband circuits, that provides quadrature outputs and is insensitive to clock phase error, with an in-band 1dB compression that is 2.4 times higher and an NF that is 1 dB lower than a state-of-the-art harmonic rejection mixer with the same number of transistors.
we have demonstrated a low-power, low-noise quadrature down-converter that provides high harmonic rejection without requiring calibration.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a two-stage harmonic rejection downconverter can be realized using a bias-current sharing approach that is simple and robust to clock phase errors.
bias current can be shared in a way that allows for the design of high performance harmonic rejection quadrature mixers without requiring additional biasing circuitry or calibration.
bias-current reuse can significantly reduce the analog power consumption of quadrature down-converters.
